native.real: original Go TLS + Rust AF_PACKET/TUN, 3 network namespaces, real original owner Stop, no m0_v4_probe
native.driver_qdisc: original owned Linux TUN tc root fq flow_limit=256, per-flow maxrate 600 vs 1500 Mbit both actual kernel tc readback
native.bulk: one real kernel TCP iperf3 stream 20s with concurrent 160 UDP and 160 TCP small echoes

decision: 600Mbit per-flow is confirmed real source limit; default1500 causes severe shared-M1 local overflow and QoS regression. Do NOT globally promote1500. Evaluate a calculated intermediate normal-only cap with service headroom or isolate sparse first-delivery path before raising persistent cap.
caveats: One native 20-second two-leg screen, not 3-leg baseline restoration; no cross-platform conclusion.
Zero artificial netem loss but 293881 native SharedTun full drops in candidate; not zero packet loss.
UDP offer-to-reply 160/160 vs 132/160; don't report p99 among survivors as successful low-latency delivery.
FQ 0 would change queue type and is not an equivalent counterfactual; both arms use the same fq and flow_limit256.
Single-flow 1064Mbps local receiver under raw Linux native VM; not physical WAN, Windows or all modes.
No general aggregate capacity/fairness solution from per-flow fq cap change alone.
